title: How did the Statue of Liberty get to New York?
sources: National Park Service Statue of Liberty History

lines.text: How did a colossal three-hundred-foot copper statue built in Paris cross the stormy Atlantic Ocean to New York Harbor?
lines.caps: How did the Statue of *Liberty | cross the stormy *ocean?

lines.text: It arrived as the world's most epic jigsaw puzzle.
lines.caps: Arrived as the world's *most epic | giant jigsaw *puzzle!

lines.text: Designed by sculptor Bartholdi with an internal iron skeleton engineered by Gustave Eiffel, it was fully assembled in Paris first.
lines.caps: Engineered by Gustave *Eiffel | and built in *Paris first

lines.text: To transport it, workers painstakingly disassembled Lady Liberty into three hundred and fifty individual pieces.
The crates were loaded aboard a French navy steamship that nearly capsized in heavy oceanic gales.
When it reached New York in eighteen eighty-five, Americans reassembled the pieces around an iron truss skeleton over four months.
lines.caps: Reassembled in *New York | over four intense *months

lines.text: Originally shiny reddish bronze, copper oxidation turned her into the iconic green monument we cherish today.
lines.caps: Oxidation turned her *bronze | into iconic emerald *green!
